summary_paragraph: A female patient with bipolar disorder, asthma, and a history of multiple suicide attempts was admitted after being found unresponsive in her car following a drug overdose involving clonidine, haloperidol, and olanzapine. She presented with altered mental status, a GCS of 8, bradycardia, and prolonged QT interval. Intubation was performed for airway protection, and she was managed in the medical unit with fluid resuscitation, electrolyte repletion, and telemetry monitoring. The metabolic acidosis and QT prolongation resolved over the course of admission. She was successfully extubated on hospital day two and regained full mental clarity. A small area of phlebitis at an IV site was noted but did not progress. She was stabilized on lithium and other supportive medications, and psychiatric evaluation recommended transfer to a long-term psychiatric facility. She was discharged medically stable and alert, with plans for continued mental health treatment.
problems: Bipolar I disorder, most recent episode (or current) depressed, unspecified
Suicide and self-inflicted poisoning by tranquilizers and other psychotropic agents
Phlebitis and thrombophlebitis of superficial veins of upper extremities
